Back to Guelph

Guelph in comparison to other institutions

Carleton

https://carleton.ca/accessibility/

                Carleton has some accessibility resources that Guelph does not appear to have, including in relationship to washrooms. Carleton University has adopted the Rick Hansen Accessibility Certification.[1] Furthermore, Carleton’s campus map also allows one to click/tap on buildings to obtain information such as washroom presence, as seen in the figure below.[2]

https://carleton.ca/campus-map/

TMU

The Toronto Metropolitan University maintains a list of single occupancy washrooms by building, including room number, floor, and a description of their accessibility features. This is great as it allows students, faculty, and broader members of the community to locate where the bathrooms they need are.[3] This furthermore serves as an example of universal design, with accessibility features aiding all while taking every user into consideration; for instance, a fully abled person may still need a baby change table, and this would help them to locate one.[4]
